title: sofo Song Form chart
description: A chord chart for a band that reads chord symbols rather than notation: one JSON document per song, rendered to a US-Letter page. Documents name this schema in their own "$schema" member, which is how the format is versioned — a breaking change ships as sf-2.schema.json rather than by editing this file. The prose spec, with the conversion guidance an author needs, is AGENTS.md at the repo root.

$schema.description: The version of this format the document follows. Files the app saves always carry it.

title.description: Large, centered at the top of the page.

key.description: Concert pitch, always — the app transposes for Bb/Eb/F/A instruments and guitar capos as a view, and never rewrites the file.

time.description: Time signature. Empty means unset; 6/8, 9/8 and 12/8 are counted in dotted quarters unless tempoUnit says otherwise.

tempo.description: BPM as a number. The empty string means unset, which is what a field cleared in the editor leaves behind.

tempoUnit.description: The note value the tempo counts, drawn as a metronome marking. Usually omitted: absent or empty means inferred from `time`. Set it only when the song contradicts that, such as a cut-time chart counted in half notes.

groove.description: The feel, in a few words: "Blues shuffle", "Four-on-the-floor disco". Renders on one line.

feel.description: Accepted alias for `groove`, kept for hand-written files. `groove` wins when both are present.

countOff.description: Who counts the band in, and how: "Drums: 4 on the hi-hat". Gets its own line.

notes.description: How the song starts, and general reminders. Printed under the header, one paragraph per entry.

sections.description: The song, in playing order. Repeated sections are duplicated rather than referenced.

endNotes.description: How the song ends: endings, repeats, cues. Printed after the last section.

updated.description: ISO 8601. Shown in the page footer; the app rewrites it on every edit.

lines.description: A block of prose as separate lines, each rendered on its own.

section.description: One named part of the song. Numbering is automatic: reuse the same `name` and the labels become Verse 1, Verse 2 — never write "verse 1" yourself.

name.description: Section type, lowercase. Drives the label, the numbering and the background tint. intro, verse, prechorus, chorus, bridge, interlude, solo, breakdown, vamp and outro get their own tint; anything else renders neutral and still works.

label.description: Overrides the displayed name. Numbering still applies.

notes.description: Cues and dynamics for this section, italic under the bars.

phrases.description: The canonical home for this section's harmony.

bars.description: Shorthand for hand-sketching: this many empty bars as a single phrase. Expanded to `phrases` on load.

chords.description: Shorthand: these bars as a single phrase. Expanded to `phrases` on load.

lyrics.description: Shorthand: moves onto this section's single phrase on load.

phrase.description: One musical line — conventionally 4 bars, sometimes 2 or 8. Phrases in a section sit side by side on one row, each as wide as its bar count, and wrap past 8 bars.

chords.description: One entry per bar. This is what makes the phrase 4 bars long.

lyrics.description: Lines of text under this phrase's bars. They only say which words go with which bars — no syllable or rhythm alignment.

bars.description: Shorthand: this many empty bars. Expanded into `chords` on load.

bar.description: One measure, where the type carries the meaning: "C" is one chord for the bar, "" keeps playing the previous chord and renders as a simile mark, and ["Dm7", "G7"] is two chords sharing the measure. Harmonic rhythm is deliberately no finer than this — the format does not model beats. A chord symbol is root + quality + optional /bass ("Abmaj7/Eb"); anything unparseable prints verbatim, so "N.C." is fine.
